sentences.text: Lorosuchus is recognized as the most basal known member of the sebecid family, a group within the unranked Mesoeucrocodylia.
The generic name combines 'Loro', referring to the Río Loro Formation, and 'suchus', a Latinized form of the Greek word for the Egyptian crocodile god Sobek.
The genus was named by Diego Pol and Jaime E. Powell in 2011, with the type species being Lorosuchus nodosus.
The species is known from holotype PVL 6219, which consists of a nearly complete skull articulated with lower jaws and fragmentary postcranial remains.
The fossils were collected at the southern end of the Medina Range, near El Cadillal Lake.
Lorosuchus lived during the Middle to Late Paleocene, approximately 61.7 to 55.8 million years ago.
The fossil record for Lorosuchus spans from 59.24 to 56 million years ago during the Thanetian stage.
